note: GET /api/v1 returns name/version/openapi/docs links. No unversioned /api root with timezone/version; trivial.
OpenAPI 3.1 JSON generated from the same route definitions the dispatcher enforces; the reference page is generated from them too.

item: Authentication: per-user DRF token + session; per-tournament permission checks (PerTournamentPermissionRequired)
note: Per-tournament tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes, per-area read/write scopes (least privilege), revocable, lastUsedAt; per-token/per-IP burst limits and durable write limits (Tabbycat has no throttling). Tokens are bound to a tournament, not a user.

item: Anonymous public read access gated by preferences (PublicPreferencePermission / IsAdminOrReadOnly / OnRelease)
tabbycat: api/permissions.py:26-46; api/views.py access_preference on each view
note: v1 requires a bearer token even for public data, so a third party needs an admin-issued read:public token. Release gating itself is equivalent (public projection). Anonymous JSON exists only as the non-REST /api/public/tournaments/{slug} projection.
Cursor pagination (limit 1-200, nextCursor) instead of limit/offset plus a Link header. The wire shape differs; the capability is the same.

Only GET and PATCH (name, short name, active) of the token's own tournament. No list, create or delete through the token API, because tokens are per tournament by design. Grep: path "/tournaments" in routes -> none.

item: Tournament preferences (list, retrieve, update, partial update, bulk)
note: Bulk partial PATCH covers update and bulk; there is no per-preference URL. Tabbycat lets anonymous users read non-sensitive prefs; CrabbyTab allows admin tokens only (minor).

item: Rounds CRUD (GET list/detail, POST, update, DELETE)
note: Status changes (release draw, reveal panels, release results, complete, silent, feedback weight, break categories) go through tab-room rules, with 409 rule_violation and override. Rounds are addressed by seq, as in Tabbycat.

item: Motions CRUD with public release filtering
note: Public tokens see motions only once they are released (public projection). Deleting a motion is refused when a ballot records it.
Read and replace-the-whole-list only: no per-question detail/POST/PATCH/DELETE and no from_adj/from_team filters. Questions are admin-only, while Tabbycat lists them publicly.

item: Feedback CRUD + filters (source_type, source, round[], target); participant URL-key submission
crabbytab: src/lib/api/v1/routes/roundData.ts:155,187 (GET, ?roundId|targetAdjudicatorId|sourceId, one at a time); src/lib/api/v1/routes/write/rounds.ts:791 (POST), 846 (PATCH confirm/ignore); src/app/api/private/sync/route.ts (participant submission, non-REST)
note: No DELETE, no source_type filter, filters cannot be combined (Firestore index limit) and there is no multi-round filter. Participants cannot submit feedback through v1 with a URL key; they can only use the private portal sync endpoint.
Read-only endpoint (score scales, plus criteria when configured). Criteria can be changed only through PATCH /preferences, not through their own CRUD endpoints.
No generic question model or endpoint. Grep: customQuestions|registrationQuestions|RegistrationQuestion in src -> none; no /questions route in src/lib/api/v1/routes.

item: Round availabilities (GET, PUT mark available, POST mark unavailable, PATCH toggle, DELETE class; ?adjudicators/teams/venues filters)
note: PUT with explicit booleans covers marking available and unavailable. There is no toggle, no bulk delete by type and no type filters on GET. Venue availability is a tournament-wide flag, not per round: a room cannot be made unavailable for one round only.

item: Pairings list/detail (GET) with public draw-release gating
note: Public tokens see draws according to the public draw mode, and panels only once revealed, as on the public site.

item: Pairings manual create / team+side edit / delete one / delete all (POST, PATCH teams, DELETE, DELETE list)
note: Through the API you cannot create a debate manually, change its teams or sides, delete a debate, or delete a round's whole draw. Regenerating with generate-draw is the only reset. Grep: DELETE on pairings paths in routes -> none.

item: Generate draw (POST /rounds/{seq}/pairings/generate-draw with draw_type + options overrides; 409 if a draw exists or is being generated)
note: Uses the tournament's draw rules only: no per-request draw_type or options (avoid_history, side_allocations, pullup, odd_bracket, pairing_method, BP assignment/position cost...). It regenerates over an existing draw (results need discardExistingResults) instead of returning 409, and records the seed. The draw type can be set per round through POST /rounds drawType.
Tabbycat's API has no allocation action. CrabbyTab runs the tab-room allocator from the API.

item: Debate ballots (list ?confirmed, create, retrieve, update confirmed/discarded, delete=discard; participant URL-key and public access)
note: Admin-token CRUD is equivalent (validated like the ballot form, aware of double entry). Missing through v1: adjudicator URL-key ballot submission and public ballot reads (ballots_released / private_ballots_released). Participants submit only through the private portal sync endpoint.
Mapped to paper-ballot receipts (ballotIntake). Only GET and PUT exist: no un-check (DELETE), toggle (PATCH) or identifier creation (POST).

item: Preformed panels (list, create, delete all, PUT add blank panels with anticipated brackets/liveness, per-panel CRUD)
note: Only a replace-all PUT. There is no 'add blank' generation of panels with calculated bracket/liveness and no per-panel endpoints. Panels carry importance, not bracket_min/max/liveness.
Includes qualification rule, institution cap, reserve size and teamOverrides, validated by validateBreakCategoryDraft.

item: Break eligibility (GET, PUT replace, PATCH add teams)
note: No add-only PATCH, and public tokens cannot read it (Tabbycat makes it public when public_break_categories is on).

item: Breaking teams (GET list, POST generate break, PATCH remark + regenerate, DELETE break)
crabbytab: src/lib/api/v1/routes/entities.ts:385 (GET, public once released); src/lib/api/v1/routes/write/rounds.ts:588 (POST generateBreak); write/rounds.ts:491 (teamOverrides on category PATCH)
note: Generate and read exist. Remarks are set as teamOverrides on the category PATCH (then POST break again), not through PATCH on /break. There is no DELETE /break to clear a generated break.

item: Speaker categories CRUD (non-public hidden from public)
Speaker category eligibility (GET, PUT replace, PATCH add)
note: No add-only PATCH, and public tokens cannot read it (Tabbycat makes it public when public_participants is on and the category is public).
List, detail, POST, PATCH and DELETE with unique name/code checks; Tabbycat's per-tournament route is list-only. Only the ?region filter is missing (region is serialized).
CrabbyTab institutions are per tournament by design (no cross-tournament institution table); per-tournament CRUD covers the use.

item: Teams CRUD (staff see unconfirmed/registration teams; public when public_participants)
note: Includes speakers, break categories and institution conflicts. Deleting a team is refused once it has debated. Public only once the participants list is released.
A speaker with recorded speeches cannot be removed.
CRUD with conflicts is equivalent. There is no ?break filter for breaking adjudicators, although Adjudicator.breaking exists (src/types/index.ts:830).

item: Person check-ins: adjudicator/speaker (GET status, PUT in, DELETE out, PATCH toggle, POST create identifier; participant URL-key self check-in)
note: No PATCH toggle and no POST identifier creation. Speakers check in through their team. Self check-in by URL key works only through the private portal endpoint, not v1. Check-in expiry is applied.
GET, PUT and DELETE only. It is a boolean flag with no timestamp/expiry and no barcode identifier creation.
Venue names must be unique.
Categories are derived from the venues' category strings. Read-only list with no detail/create/update/delete; change a category through each venue's category field.
CrabbyTab has schedule events (docs/api.md wrongly says 'no such models yet') and anonymous public JSON + iCal, but no v1 token endpoints to list or edit them.
Ranked by the configured precedence, with every metric returned; ?round is admin-only. Missing the ?category (break-category) filter and the per-request metrics/extra_metrics override.
No endpoint gives per-round wins/points for past non-silent rounds before the tab is released. Grep: current-rounds|currentStandings in src -> none.

item: Speaker standings substantive + replies (?category, ?round, ?metrics; missed-debates rank filter)
note: Missed-speech ineligibility (rank 0, ineligible flag) and precedence are present. Missing the ?category (speaker category) filter and the metrics override.
Substantive scores by round only; no replies or ghost query options.

item: Adjudicator standings (base, final weighted score, per-round feedback)
note: Requires read:standings + read:feedback. Not public even when the adjudicator tab is released (Tabbycat: public when adjudicators_tab_released). Minor.
Staff roles are managed through session-authenticated internal routes, not the token API; v1 has no group model endpoint.
Accounts are Firebase Auth identities; site-wide user administration is out of scope for per-tournament tokens.

item: Participant identification /me by private URL key
note: Same 'Authorization: Key' scheme plus a passcode and a durable limit of 120 attempts per IP per hour. An unknown key and a wrong passcode get the same 401.
No browser push notifications. Grep: webpush|PushManager|pushSubscription in src -> none (CrabbyTab notifies by email).

item: Action logging of API writes (APILogActionMixin, agent=API)
note: Audit events carry the token id/name and the request id. Every write is one Firestore transaction with versioned archives and expectedVersion optimistic concurrency, which Tabbycat lacks.
API writes run the same tab-room commands and rules as the UI (409 rule_violation, with override reasons recorded). Unknown fields are rejected (422).
